name: ChessMate
tagline: A real chessboard whose pieces move by themselves, so a remote player can face someone at the board, with coaching and voice control.
problem: Playing chess with family abroad means giving up the physical board, and moving pieces is hard for people with limited mobility or vision.
solution: A two-axis gantry under the board moves magnetized pieces with an electromagnet. A Raspberry Pi watches the board through a webcam, runs a chess engine and a collision-free pathfinding routine, and sends moves to an Arduino driving stepper motors. A web app adds AI coaching and voice commands.
demo_moment: Team-described: a move made in the web app or by voice slides the real piece across the board.

why_it_stood_out.claim: Selected by the organizer as one of 12 finalists among 261 submissions.
Motivated by the team's own families: playing chess across countries.
Combines a custom gantry, vision, a chess engine and pathfinding; the team says the second axis and piece detection took most of the weekend.
A board that moves on its own is a familiar object doing something surprising, which is easy to remember after a day of demos.

lessons: Hardware takes longer than planned: two subsystems took most of the event, so schedule integration time first.
